entries.paired_script_result: The complete Latin and Kana values were compared word by word, including person prefixes, gemination/final consonants, nominalizer p, X/Y, pixel, numbers, quotation marks and punctuation. No lexical or logical difference was detected.
entries.note: Accepted as a descriptive numeric-positioning label. The complete head-final phrase makes uske the placement location, anu the placement action, and the written-number NP the standard for the intensified koracipo modifier of that action. This is not a claim that koracipo is a lexical translation of mathematical precision or that a location is itself a number. In the X/Y form, exact conformity to entered numbers is the relevant kind of exact positioning.
connected_language_assessment: The relative a=nuye clause modifies cipiskip. The resulting NP is a valid nominal complement to koracipo; it is not a finite clause mistakenly attached to a nominal-only postposition.

koracipo is an attested intensified correspondence construction. The primary koraci material also gives an accordance-with-words use, so this family is not confined to resemblance of two physical objects. Reading written coordinates as instructions/specifications is a transparent contextual extension of that construction.

The complete a=anu uske head and its preceding manner phrase label a location established in exact accordance with written numeric values. The precision component is attached to placing, not to how neatly the digits are written.
No claim is made that this is a conventional short Ainu term for precision, or that this wording should replace unrelated exact-position labels outside a numerical positioning form.
resolved_holds: The old un-intensified correspondence-only reading is resolved by attested koracipo and a complete placement-location parse in the given numeric UI context.
remaining_uncertainty: Idiomatic preference among alternative technical labels; no native-speaker endorsement.

entries.source: Set the top-left corner of this image on the output canvas. X and Y are whole pixels, starting at zero. Other images keep their current positions. Overlap is allowed here; images imported later are drawn on top. The canvas expands to include all placed images. Crops and sizes stay unchanged.
entries.target: A=sanke noka a=nuye uske or ta, tan noka tuyka un sikkewe, harkisama ta an pe, anu yan. X ka Y ka, 「0, 1, 2, 3, …」 or wa a=numke cipiskip ne; pixel ani, 0 wano a=piski. Mosma noka a=ari uske anak a=sinnare ka somo ki. Te ta noka a=ukaomare yakka pirka; oka ta a=omare noka anak hoski a=omare noka ka ta a=nuye. A=ari noka opitta anak noka a=nuye uske onnay ta oka kuni, noka a=nuye uske poro. A=tuye uske ka noka kor pororu ka a=sinnare ka somo ki.
entries.paired_script_result: The complete Latin and Kana values were compared word by word, including person prefixes, gemination/final consonants, nominalizer p, X/Y, pixel, numbers, quotation marks and punctuation. No lexical or logical difference was detected.
entries.note: The full paragraph has materially improved and most former holds are closed. However, the first command still depends on a post-head apposition and an implicit third-person possessor for harkisama. I cannot establish with sufficient confidence that its left-side phrase restricts the upper corner of this same image, rather than taking a different nearby referent. The intended top-left is recoverable, but that is not enough for complete-value acceptance. This is an uncertainty hold, not a demonstrated claim that Ainu apposition is ungrammatical.
connected_language_assessment: The opening output drawing-place phrase functions as the placement location. The following tan noka tuyka un sikkewe supplies an upper-edge corner; the comma-separated harkisama ta an pe then attempts to identify the left one. un supports an attributive locative phrase, and pe supports a headless relative. Neither fact alone determines the possessor/antecedent of harkisama across this particular apposition.

The number sentence now uses actual chosen-number membership, followed by pixel units and a zero-origin counting clause. The same source-plus-selection evidence that clears the standalone validation also clears this local grammatical issue. The help need not repeat the validation upper bound.

Negating changes to the placement locations of other images now expresses position invariance directly. ari is plural placement. The derived change verb uses productive causative morphology over sinna, and the ka somo ki construction negates the event; it is descriptive application behavior, not a prohibition addressed to the user.

The overlap permission and later-versus-earlier drawing relation stay distinct. ka in the layer clause supplies a surface/stacking relation, whereas tuyka in the first command refers to the upper edge. There is no reversal of import order.

The expansion clause now explicitly topicalizes all placed images and supplies the drawing-place NP immediately before onnay. That NP is the container; the images are the plural subject of oka. The main-clause subject is the same drawing place and poro supplies enlargement. The purpose dependency therefore grows the canvas to contain the images without resizing the images.

The final repeated-ka coordination scopes crop/place and image size under the unchanged predicate together. Crop/place and pororu remain descriptive modern technical terminology; the technical nature of those words is not itself a grammatical defect.

entries.source: X and Y must be whole numbers from zero to 2147483647.
entries.target: X ka Y ka, 「0, 1, 2, 3, …, 2147483647」 or wa a=numke cipiskip ne kuni p ne.
entries.paired_script_result: The complete Latin and Kana values were compared word by word, including person prefixes, gemination/final consonants, nominalizer p, X/Y, pixel, numbers, quotation marks and punctuation. No lexical or logical difference was detected.
entries.note: Accepted as one complete validation message. Both X and Y are predicated as a chosen numeric value from the explicitly bounded unit-step enumeration, with the normative kuni p ne frame applying to the whole predicate. The number list is a quoted object/domain of selection rather than the subject of an agentive passive. This accepts a transparent technical extension of attested source-plus-selection syntax; it does not pretend that a historical corpus used this software limit.
connected_language_assessment: Repeated ka coordinates X and Y under one predicate and applies the requirement to both. No grammatical operation makes them a pair that must share one identical coordinate value.

The primary Kawakami Matsuko transcript directly combines a container-source or wa phrase with numke. Together with the productive noun-to-location use of or, this supports selection out of the displayed numeric domain. The new application is to an abstract written collection, which is explicitly acknowledged.
The selected-number relative clause is supported by numke usage and the nominal head cipiskip. The quoted sequence is not itself asserted to be a single number.

The visible progression 0, 1, 2, 3, …, 2147483647 includes zero and the final integer, advances in units, and ends at the stated bound. Fractions, negatives and values above the bound are not members. Ellipsis is mathematical enumeration, not omitted translation.

kuni p ne supplies the expected/required-state assertion at the end of the complete copular proposition. Primary kuni evidence explicitly includes obligation, and the nominalized normative frame is attested. This is stronger evidence than merely reading the final ne as a bare identity predicate.
resolved_holds: Source-plus-selection construction has primary speaker-transcript evidence.
Normative kuni p ne is attested and appropriate to the complete validation proposition.
remaining_uncertainty: The numeric collection is a modern compositional extension, not an attested traditional example or standardized mathematical idiom.

P1.short_exact_evidence: kor itanki or wa kam pirka uske numke wa
P1.evidence: The speaker selects a good portion of meat from a bowl. This directly attests source or wa with numke. Extending the source to a written numeric collection is the reviewer’s compositional judgment, not a claim that this example contains mathematics.

C1.evidence: cipiskip is published for number; omare/sanke are published computing import/export terms; pororu is explicitly a coined size term. Publication is not broad community endorsement.

The earlier six accepted X/Y/unknown-image originals are outside this review; their prior verdicts are unchanged.

important_negative_findings: A source-assisted compositional review does not require a historical attestation of every software phrase.
Attested source-plus-selection grammar closes the validation hold, while the abstract numeric-domain application is explicitly an inference.
Correct Latin/Kana correspondence is verified but never substitutes for the linguistic verdict.
The help hold is specifically referential/structural; supported purpose, enlargement, permission, numerical-domain and invariance clauses should not be repeatedly rejected.
